complete_retained_gap_set.topic: Any-player permission to limit Spirit Phase deliberation time
complete_retained_gap_set.proposed_question: Under The Urgency of War, is setting a limit on the time available to complete the Spirit Phase reserved for the game owner/organizer, or may any player set such a limit?
complete_retained_gap_set.predetermined_answer: Any player may set a limit on the time available to complete the Spirit Phase.

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: Who may set the Spirit Phase time limit?
required_facts: Any player may set that limit; it is not reserved for the owner/organizer.

key_context_not_required.fact: The book gives a timer, a stated condition or another desired means as examples.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The question asks actor permission, not examples, duration, tool, etiquette, or an automatic penalty.

key_context_not_required.fact: This permission does not supply a rule for deleting unpaid cards, declaring defeat, or resolving unfinished choices when a clock expires.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: No such consequence is printed or asked; do not invent one.

primary_sources.locator: CORE p8, The Urgency of War, complete sidebar; fresh source slice[16000,22000)
primary_sources.complete_source_delivery: Own immutable complete original source ledger; targeted fresh ranges in current ledger when applicable.

complete_retained_gap_set.primary_passage:
THE URGENCY OF WAR
Some Spirits are inclined to take a long time
choosing Power Cards: perhaps several centuries in
the case of slow-moving earth Spirits. But the threat
of the Invaders forbids the luxury of infinite time.
Any player may place a limit on the time available
to complete the Spirit Phase. This can be done using
a timer, setting a condition (“When I get back, we 
start”), or any other means desired.
Of course, as this is a cooperative game, it behooves
you to not be too draconian.
complete_retained_gap_set.producer_proof: This is an express ordinary rulebook procedure/actor permission, not a granted new Power modifier, trigger or imported component. It needs no effect producer beyond the actual CORE p8 permission.

actual_prompt_overlap_assessment.difference: Q55 tests decision ownership and consensus fallbacks, including organizer fallback for non-land decisions. It never asks who may set a Spirit Phase time limit, and its fallback does not test the specific any-player permission.
No time-limit actor permission is requested.

actual_prompt_overlap_assessment.difference: No time-limit actor permission is requested.

The sidebar is in ordinary Sequence of Play, not optional difficulty/scoring or an expansion. It concerns table pacing rather than a state-changing Power; that boundary is disclosed for coordinator adjudication, not hidden by inventing an engine effect. If the benchmark explicitly excludes all table-administration permissions, it should be rejected on that explicit scope ground rather than described as tested.
